newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 10.

text.p: PRAVO - The Slovak Republic still owes 11 billion crowns to Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. According to experts, non payment of the debt is only one step Slovakia is taking to pressure the Czech Republic into erase debts totalling 24 billion crowns.
- The Czech Social Democratic Party insists that the privatisation of hospitals should be stopped until health care and health insurance are readily available to all.
- There were 106,275 accidents in the workplace in the Czech Republic last year, 281 of which were fatal.

- Austrian steel concern Voest-Alpine has announced its intention to invest in Ostrava's Nova Hut. The company will wait to see how the privatisation of Nova Hut progresses before making any final decisions.
- Centrotex won the public tender for 42.15 percent of Textilany Liberec.
- Poldi Steel sro, which has not been producing since February, intends to begin production on December 1 according to general manager, Vladimir Stehlik.
- The president of TelSource, Bessel Kok, was voted onto the supervisory board of Banka Hana as the workers' representative.

- Aliatel a.s., a new telecommunications company, has obtained a license to offer public telephone services. "This allows us to liberalise the market, starting in 2001, by competing with the current monopoly, SPT Telecom," according to the general manager of Aliatel, Frantisek Valek.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The general director and chairman of the board of Unipetrol, Miroslav Tera, has been given two days to offer his resignation. Tera himself replaced the vice-minister of finance last year.

- The current account deficit, currently at seven percent of GDP and likely to increase to eight percent in 1997, is risky for the further economic developmentof the country according to an analysis from the Patria Finance investment company.

- A proposal to combine the second and third trade groups on the Prague Stock Market starting at the beginning of next year was accepted yesterday by the Council for Stock Exchange Trade. All issues will begin trading daily from this date.
